description: Patients none of whose lab records has a U-PRO result of '-'.

a.request: For patients none of whose laboratory records has a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of '-', first take each patient's average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average alkaline phosphatase-to-ALT ratio (`ALP` ÷ `GPT`, per record) across all their lab records. Then, for each sex (`SEX` from the Patient table, with a blank value as its own group), report the sex and the averages of those per-patient averages. Only lab records with a matching Patient record count. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS excluded WHERE excluded.ID = p.ID AND excluded.`U-PRO` = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_alp_gpt_ratio) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM patient_averages GROUP BY SEX

c.request: Looking only at patients without a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of '-' in their lab tests, what are the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average alkaline phosphatase-to-ALT ratio (`ALP` ÷ `GPT`, per record) by sex? Compute each patient's averages over all their lab records first, then average those per-patient figures within each sex (`SEX` from the Patient table, with a blank value as its own group). Only count lab records that match a Patient record, ignore missing values in the averages and don't round. Patients none of whose lab records has a U-PRO result of '-'.
c.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(1.0 * l.ALP / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS x WHERE x.ID = p.ID AND x.`U-PRO` = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_alp_gpt_ratio) AS avg_alp_gpt_ratio FROM patient_averages GROUP BY SEX;

b.request: For patients with no lab record where `U-PRO` is `'-'`, calculate each patient’s average nonmissing `PT` and average per-record `ALP` ÷ `GPT` using lab records matched to `Patient`; then average those patient-level values by `SEX`, treating blank sex as its own group, without rounding.
b.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_alp_gpt FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS x WHERE x.ID = p.ID AND x.`U-PRO` = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_alp_gpt) AS avg_alp_gpt FROM patient_averages GROUP BY SEX
b.raw: For patients with no lab record where `U-PRO` is `'-'`, calculate each patient’s average nonmissing `PT` and average per-record `ALP` ÷ `GPT` using lab records matched to `Patient`; then average those patient-level values by `SEX`, treating blank sex as its own group, without rounding.

d.request: For each sex, including blank SEX as its own group, select patients with no lab record where `U-PRO` is `'-'`; using only lab records matched to a Patient record, calculate each selected patient’s average nonmissing `PT` and average nonmissing per-record `ALP` ÷ `GPT`, then average those patient-level values within each sex without rounding.
d.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(1.0 * l.ALP / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_alp_gpt FROM Patient AS p LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS excluded WHERE excluded.ID = p.ID AND excluded.`U-PRO` = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_patient_pt, AVG(avg_alp_gpt) AS avg_patient_alp_gpt FROM patient_averages GROUP BY SEX
